title: Saudi Pro League writes to clubs insisting games to continue despite Middle East conflict
content:
The Saudi Pro League (SPL) has written to its clubs informing them that matches will go ahead despite the escalation of conflict in the Middle East.

The U.S. embassy in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh was the subject of a drone attack by Iran earlier this week, according to the Saudi Ministry of Defence. The King Fahd Causeway, which connects Saudi Arabia with Bahrain, has also been targeted.

The Athletic has spoken to SPL staff members who asked to remain anonymous as they weren’t permitted to speak publicly.

One said that there was a growing sense of unease among players and staff regarding their safety following the events of recent days, while another source said many players’ families had left the region due to safety concerns.

“The SPL have sent out a letter to clubs saying it’s safe to keep playing but a lot of people here are unconvinced,” the first staff member said.

“A lot of the foreign players just want to get out of the region. Some have already managed to get their families out. It’s shaken people up.

“There’s a contradiction between the SPL claiming we’re safe to play and the national danger alerts that are being sent out about staying away from the bridge and certain buildings.

“We’re still training normally and we’re being told the games this weekend will go ahead but things could change if players start pulling out. I don’t see how they can guarantee our safety.”

The SPL’s letter informed clubs that security protocols were being followed and that matches will continue, although the situation continues to be monitored day by day.

The SPL has been contacted by The Athletic for comment.

The next round of SPL games kicks off on Thursday with Al Kholood against Al Qadsiah and Damac against Al Riyadh.

Leaders Al Nassr are scheduled to face Neom on Saturday. They were due to face Al Wasl in the Asian Champions League Two on Wednesday but matches in that competition have been cancelled due to the conflict in the region.

Other states in the region have postponed matches in reaction to the escalating conflict, which began when the U.S. and Israel launched missile strikes on major Iranian cities last Saturday.

Qatar has cancelled all matches until further notice and there is growing uncertainty whether the Finalissima between Spain and Argentina — the reigning European and Copa America champions respectively — will go ahead as planned in Doha on March 27.

The Asian Football Confederation has also postponed matches in the AFC Champions League.

Newcastle United defender Fabian Schar has returned from Dubai to England, having been in the city completing rehab work as he recovers from an ankle injury. Schar confirmed he had returned “safely” in a post on Instagram and described the experience as “terrifying”.
